title: [CRY2-9] `channelToken` derived from the admission seed mixes two uses of one secret and conflicts
description: Review finding CRY2-9: `channelToken` derived from the admission seed mixes two uses of one secret and conflicts with the HSM guidance (lens CRY2). Location: spec/12-security.md:167 (the part that holds); spec/05-messaging.md:255, spec/13-encoding.md:148 (rejected part). Fix: I reject the key-separation part. Deriving a token with HKDF under its own `info` label from a uniformly random 32-byte seed, which RFC 8032 separately hashes with SHA-512, has no attack. The reviewer says "There is no known attack", and the derivation is recorded design (ARCHITECTURE.md:241-243). The HSM conflict is real but independent of how the token is derived. 12-security.md:167 lists "the channel admission private keys the registration service issues" for HSM custody, yet 03-spaces.md:297 and 05:254 serve `seed` to every member. Fix: remove admission keys from the §12.8 HSM list and say that they are secrets shared with all current members, so hardware custody at the CO adds nothing. Full text: notes/review2/CRY2-verified.md and notes/review2/CRY2.md.
